A3 adds the business case for automation to its robotics course

A new investment-assessment module helps learners decide where industrial robotics can create value and how to evaluate a project.

RoboticsTomorrow ↗17 September 2026English editorial summary
Story

Connecting robotics with business decisions

The Association for Advancing Automation, or A3, added a business-case module to its Introduction to Industrial Robotics course. It is intended to help learners identify where automation is appropriate and assess the value of a proposed investment.

Designed for newcomers

The self-paced course does not require a technical background. It is aimed at people entering the field, operations staff and others involved in business decisions about deploying robotics.

Looking beyond the robot purchase price

The new material covers project costs, returns and payback periods, opportunities to improve productivity and quality, and workforce implications. It also addresses early project planning, requests for proposals and selecting an integrator.

Applying the ideas to a real project

Learners can use A3’s Robot System Value Calculator to assess a system they are considering. The central idea is to begin with the problem that needs solving and then examine how technology could deliver a return.
